{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Philippine government agencies report 4,948 suspected drug users and dealers, including 60 children, died during police operations from July 1st, 2016 to September 30, 2018.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Philippine National Police report 22,983 deaths classified as “homicides under investigation” since the “War on Drugs” began.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Filipinos with actual drug addiction problems or histories of drug use are used as scapegoats, criminalized, and made targets by military and police.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Filipinos with actual drug addiction problems or histories of drug use are suffering immensely under regime policies.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Funding is used to systematically murder people, instead of directing funds to services to give medical and psychological help to those living with drug addiction.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Extra-judicial killings in the Philippines, including those committed in the conduct of the anti-drug campaign, erode confidence in the Government of the Philippines’ commitment to human rights, due process, and the rule of law.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. government continues to allocate money to the Philippines through Appropriations for the Department of State, and Foreign Operations and Related Programs.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"Current annual appropriations for the Philippine military amount to $184.5 million.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
